note: PHASE 1 -- the lazy accessor + the two structural blockers. Ships getSupabase(): a memoised, safeDynamicImport-routed `import('./client')` placed BESIDE the generated client (client.ts carries a do-not-edit banner and is rewritten by regeneration, which would silently drop anything added inside it). Converts the only two sites repo-wide that structurally blocked a lazy accessor -- useOpenRaffles.ts and raffleWaVerify.ts, both `supabase.rpc.bind(supabase)` at module scope, which constructed the client as a side effect of importing the module. MEASUREMENT, stated once: post-P1 home is 244.3 KB gz / 61 chunks / 3 pullers and event is 363.8 KB / 89 chunks / 4 pullers. Against P0's 138390a baseline (244.2 / 363.5) that is +0.1 and +0.3 KB -- chunk-layout noise, NOT a regression, and the arc's actual metric (the puller SETS) is byte-identical: home = _lazyWithRetry + root + home, event = _index + _lazyWithRetry + root + event. P2 should diff against 244.3/363.8, not 244.2/363.5. STILL A STATIC EDGE, do not misread this phase: RaffleEntryDialog.tsx -- the sole consumer of raffleWaVerify, and IN the event page's first-load graph -- still holds `import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase'`, so converting raffleWaVerify removed no edge from that chunk. Its two uses sit in async handlers, so nothing structurally blocks converting it; it is simply not in P1's stated scope. useOpenRaffles lands in the lazy Raffles-* chunk and is in neither first-load graph. HYDRATION INVARIANT (unchanged, and P1 is the first phase that could have broken it): nothing may move auth state into the first render. P1 touches no auth path -- the accessor is called only from async React Query queryFns and async helpers, never during render -- so the first client render is byte-identical. TYPING NOTE later phases must copy: the accessor's type is `(typeof import('./client'))['supabase']`, erased at compile time. Importing SupabaseClient from '@supabase/supabase-js' in VALUE position would hold open the very edge this arc removes -- the same trap P4 faces with useAuth.tsx's `import { User, Session }`. TESTING NOTES, both learned the hard way here: (1) counting client constructions through a vi.mock factory proves nothing, because vitest caches the mocked module -- and asserting RESOLVED-VALUE identity is equally hollow for the same reason. The only honest memo discriminator is PROMISE IDENTITY. (2) vitest caches a SUCCESSFUL mock instantiation but re-runs a THROWING one, so the resolve-without-an-export shape cannot be sequenced with the throw shape in one file; each failure shape needs its own file with one hoisted mock, which also removes the doMock/doUnmock leak. All four accessor behaviours are mutation-proven: removing the memo fails 2 cases, a bare import() fails the stale-chunk case, dropping the presence check fails the missing-export case, and caching the rejection fails 2.
